question: Who has to pay the traffic toll fee in Dubai?
reference: The RTA charges a Traffic Toll Fee to owners of motor vehicles that use the road network of the Emirate and pass through a Traffic Toll Gate in one direction, whether or not the vehicle is registered in the Emirate.
answer: The traffic toll fee in Dubai is required to be paid by vehicle owners whose vehicles pass through Traffic Toll Gates in one direction, regardless of whether the vehicle is registered in the Emirate or not. This fee is charged by the RTA for the use of the road network of the Emirate. There are exemptions for certain vehicles such as those of societies and centres for people with special needs, vehicles of the Awqaf and Minors Affairs Foundation in Dubai, vehicles intended for use by persons with special needs, and buses used for transportation of staff and workers as prescribed by the RTA. Motor vehicles may not pass through Traffic Toll Gates without payment of the toll fees through subscription to the Salik System.

question: What is the fine for passing through a traffic toll gate without paying the prescribed charges?
reference: The fine for passing through a Traffic Toll Gate without paying the prescribed charges is 100.00 dirhams.
answer:
The fine for passing through a traffic toll gate without paying the prescribed charges in the Emirate of Dubai is **100 Dirhams** according to the Executive Council Resolution No. (19) of 2010.

There is also a provision in the Administrative Resolution No. (311) of 2007 (not in force) that specifies a daily fine escalating with repeated violations: 100 Dirhams for the first day, 200 Dirhams for the second day, and 400 Dirhams for the third or subsequent days.

Additionally, Law No. (22) of 2006 states a general penalty for violations of the Traffic Toll Law of not less than 500 Dirhams and not more than 10,000 Dirhams, with the fine doubled upon repetition within one year, but this is a broader penalty and not specific to the toll gate passage without payment.

question: How much is the Dubai airports departure fee and which passengers are exempt from it?
reference: The departure fee is seventy-five dirhams (AED 75.00) for every passenger departing the United Arab Emirates through Dubai airports. Exempt are: passengers below the age of two years; on-duty pilots and cabin crew; transit passengers whose arrival and departure flight number is the same; and transfer passengers whose final destination is not the United Arab Emirates and whose departure is within twenty-four hours of arrival.
contexts:
Law No. (13) of 2022 Concerning the Dubai Airports Departure Fee
Article (1): Charging the Fee
a. A departure fee of seventy-five dirhams (AED 75.00) will be collected from every passenger departing the United Arab Emirates through Dubai airports.
b. The following categories are hereby exempted from payment of the fee referred to in paragraph (a) of this Article:
1. passengers below the age of two (2) years;
2. on-duty pilots and cabin crew;
3. transit passengers whose arrival and departure flight number is the same ; and 4. transfer passengers whose final destination is not the United Arab Emirates and whose departure is within twenty-four (24) hours from the time of arrival.

Law No. (13) of 2022 Concerning the Dubai Airports Departure Fee
Article (3): Fee Payment
The fee collected pursuant to this Law will be paid to the Public Treasury of the Government of Dubai.

Law No. (13) of 2022 Concerning the Dubai Airports Departure Fee
Article (2): Collection of the Fee
Airlines operating in Dubai airports will be responsible for collecting the fee referred to in Article (1) of this Law upon issuing air tickets to customers within or outside of the United Arab Emirates.
The airlines must transfer the proceeds generated from collecting such a fee to the Corporation, in accordance with the processes, procedures, and time frames stipulated in the document stating the conditions for using airports, as adopted by the Corporation in this respect.

Law No. (13) of 2022 Concerning the Dubai Airports Departure Fee
Article (6): Publication and Commencement

reference: Airlines operating in Dubai airports collect the fee when issuing air tickets and must transfer the proceeds to the Corporation. The fee is paid to the Public Treasury of the Government of Dubai.

The money collected from this fee is then paid to the Public Treasury of the Government of Dubai.

question: Can an autonomous vehicle travel on a road in Dubai without being licensed by the RTA?
reference: No. No Autonomous Vehicle may travel on a Road unless it is licensed by the RTA. An Autonomous Vehicle licensed by another licensing entity in the UAE may not travel within the Emirate without first obtaining the Permit from the RTA.
answer:
An autonomous vehicle may not travel on a road in Dubai unless it is licensed by the RTA. The license is issued according to the conditions and procedures prescribed by the relevant legislation and resolutions. Additionally, if the vehicle is licensed by another UAE entity, it still requires a permit from the RTA to travel within Dubai. Therefore, traveling without RTA licensing is not permitted.

To be licensed, an autonomous vehicle must meet several conditions including being sourced from an authorized local agent, passing technical inspection, meeting safety and security standards, and being insured as prescribed by the RTA.

Furthermore, during the third phase of autonomous vehicle operation, operators must obtain the relevant permit from the RTA before operating autonomous vehicles.

question: Who is liable for damage caused by an autonomous vehicle?
reference: The Operator is liable for compensating for any damage to property or harm to individuals caused by the Autonomous Vehicle, without prejudice to the Operator's right of recourse against the person actually responsible. The RTA is not liable to third parties for damage they sustain as a result of using Autonomous Vehicles.
answer: The Operator of an Autonomous Vehicle is liable for compensating any damage to property or harm to individuals caused by the Autonomous Vehicle. The Operator has the right to seek recourse against the person actually responsible for the damage according to general liability rules. The Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) is not liable to third parties for any damage resulting from the use of Autonomous Vehicles. This liability framework is established under Law No. (9) of 2023 Regulating the Operation of Autonomous Vehicles in the Emirate of Dubai, Article 14. Additionally, the Operator has several obligations related to the operation, maintenance, and safety of the Autonomous Vehicle to ensure compliance and safe operation, as detailed in the Implementing Bylaw of the same law.

question: What are the peak hours on weekdays during which the parking fee applies?
reference: On weekdays (Monday to Saturday) the peak hours are from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. and from 4:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m.
answer:
The peak hours on weekdays (Monday to Saturday) during which the parking fee applies in the Emirate of Dubai are:
- From 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m.
- From 4:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m.
These hours are specified in Administrative Resolution No. (363) of 2026 concerning the rules for designating peak hours for parking fees.

question: Is a permit required to pilot or use an unmanned aircraft in Dubai, and who issues it?
reference: Yes. No person may pilot or use Unmanned Aircraft in the Emirate without first obtaining the relevant Permit from the DCAA (Dubai Civil Aviation Authority).
answer: A permit is required to pilot or use an unmanned aircraft in Dubai. This permit must be obtained from the Dubai Civil Aviation Authority (DCAA) before piloting, using, conducting operations, or related activities involving unmanned aircraft in the Emirate. The DCAA also considers risk assessments, the purpose of use, and the area of operation when issuing such permits to ensure safety and security. Additionally, permits are required for operating unmanned aircraft, assisting in their operation, or performing related work, and these permits are issued by the DCAA based on qualifications and specific categories determined by the Director General. Permits are also required for establishing infrastructure, airports, or supplying fuel for unmanned aircraft, all issued by the DCAA in coordination with relevant entities like the Dubai Aviation Engineering Projects Corporation.
contexts:
Law No. (4) of 2020 Regulating Unmanned Aircraft in the Emirate of Dubai
Article (10): Obtaining Permits
a. No Person may pilot or use Unmanned Aircraft; conduct Operations or Related Activities; or construct any Infrastructure or Unmanned Aircraft Airport in the Emirate, without first obtaining the relevant Permit from the DCAA. The resolutions issued in implementation of this Law will determine the conditions and requirements for issuing such a Permit.
b. When issuing the Permit referred to in paragraph (a) of this Article, the assessment of risks resulting from the operation of Unmanned Aircraft; the purpose of using them; the area where they will be used; and any other considerations the DCAA deems necessary must be taken into account to ensure the safety of air navigation and security of Operations.

Law No. (4) of 2020 Regulating Unmanned Aircraft in the Emirate of Dubai
Article (21): Establishing and Operating Unmanned Aircraft Airports
No Person may establish or operate Unmanned Aircraft Airports or make any modification thereto without first obtaining the relevant Permit from the DCAA. This Permit will be issued in coordination with the Dubai Aviation Engineering Projects Corporation and the concerned entities as per the relevant conditions and requirements approved by the DCAA and these entities.

Law No. (4) of 2020 Regulating Unmanned Aircraft in the Emirate of Dubai
Article (18): Persons Authorised to Control Unmanned Aircraft
a. No Person may operate, assist in operating, or monitor the operation of Unmanned Aircraft or perform any work related to their operating systems unless that Person is qualified to do so and holds a relevant Permit from the DCAA.
b. The Director General will, pursuant to a resolution he issues in this respect and based on the type of Unmanned Aircraft and their control systems, determine the categories of, and the requirements and procedures for issuing, the Permit referred to in paragraph (a) of this Article for an Unmanned Aircraft Pilot, a Controller, or a Crew Member.

Law No. (4) of 2020 Regulating Unmanned Aircraft in the Emirate of Dubai
Article (20): Establishment of Infrastructure
The Infrastructure required for conducting Unmanned Aircraft Operations may not be established without first obtaining the relevant Permit from the DCAA. This Permit will be issued in coordination with the Dubai Aviation Engineering Projects Corporation and the concerned entities as per the relevant conditions and requirements approved by the DCAA and these entities.

Law No. (4) of 2020 Regulating Unmanned Aircraft in the Emirate of Dubai
Article (23): Fuel and Power Supply
No entity may supply Unmanned Aircraft with fuel or power without first obtaining the relevant Permit from the DCAA. This Permit will be issued in coordination with the Dubai Aviation Engineering Projects Corporation and the concerned entities as per the relevant conditions and requirements approved by the DCAA and these entities.
